I will start from what people around me do here in Quzhou, then I will adjust a bit by crop value and by how much money I can afford to press into 200 mu. I have only farmed 4 years, so I do not like making big jumps. Wheat and maize are still my backbone, because that is the steady part of the land and I know the water from the well can hold them up if the rain is short. On wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because if wheat stools weak in spring, it is hard to pull yield back later. On maize, I will keep the stand dense and feed it enough nitrogen, because if the ears do not set well, the whole season is wasted. Cabbage takes more fertilizer, more water, and more spraying, but the cash return is better, so I will put it on a smaller area that I can watch closely. Stevia also needs cleaner field management, so I will keep it in a moderate area, not too much, so I can manage weeds, topping, and harvest properly. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch yield fall, but I still have to leave room in the budget for pesticide, irrigation electricity, and hired labor at busy times.
